title: Expected false wakes per month vs per-window rejection
caption: Packet-owned illustration of the book's margin arithmetic: ~2.59M non-keyword windows/month means even 99.999% per-window rejection leaves ~26 expected false wakes — 26x over a one-per-month budget. Against the 1/month budget this shows why commercial assistants add a second, larger verification stage rather than asking the always-on detector to meet the bound alone.

title: Remediation backlog growth at constant net rates
caption: Illustrative compounding of a 100-engineer-hour data-debt backlog over a 12-month planning window at net growth rates of 10%, 20%, and 30%. The formula is the book's planning heuristic — real backlogs jump at discrete upstream migrations rather than compounding smoothly.
